reason: Both conversations correctly identified the crushed, fluff-filled vent hose as the overheating cause, avoided blaming the thermostat before airflow was proved, and sensibly pointed the tenant to the landlord. Conversation 1 was tighter on the safety boundary (unplug before working, don't run it while the hose is crushed or if the cabinet gets excessively hot again, clear escalation path if it persists) and never pushed a parts lookup for a fault that needs no internal part. Conversation 2 did obtain a nice confirming test (ran 40 min with the hose off) and gave a reasonable 'not necessarily a new hose' answer, but it inserted an unnecessary model-number panel to 'check a suitable replacement' when no part was justified, and its 'check the wall vent outside' slightly ignored the stated window-vent setup.
